problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over a 20-week operational cycle.  
The initial stockpile at the cycle’s commencement is 72 thousand liters.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 20 \), the supplier permits the company to submit a procurement request, the volume of which must fall between 16 and 32 thousand liters.  
Nevertheless, every request issued will require 1 week for transit before it becomes available to meet consumption or replenish reserves.  
The weekly consumption of the additive is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: 29 thousand liters  
* Week 2: 15 thousand liters  
* Week 3: 33 thousand liters  
* Week 4: 19 thousand liters  
* Week 5: 38 thousand liters  
* Week 6: 11 thousand liters  
* Week 7: 34 thousand liters  
* Week 8: 51 thousand liters  
* Week 9: 38 thousand liters  
* Week 10: 13 thousand liters  
* Week 11: 50 thousand liters  
* Week 12: 59 thousand liters  
* Week 13: 59 thousand liters  
* Week 14: 28 thousand liters  
* Week 15: 42 thousand liters  
* Week 16: 49 thousand liters  
* Week 17: 59 thousand liters  
* Week 18: 37 thousand liters  
* Week 19: 39 thousand liters  
* Week 20: 49 thousand liters  

Stockouts are tolerated, yet any unsatisfied consumption is considered lost and will not be deferred.  
Throughout the 20-week horizon, additive quantities may be treated as continuous, and the aggregate volume of fuel additive held in storage at any moment must not surpass the depot’s capacity of 72 thousand liters.  
The cumulative expense over the planning cycle comprises three elements: the procurement expense, amounting to 1 monetary unit per thousand liters ordered; the storage expense, amounting to 2 monetary units per thousand liters of stock transferred from one week to the next; and the shortage penalty, amounting to 7 monetary units per thousand liters of unfulfilled consumption.  
The objective is to ascertain the optimal procurement volume for each week and monitor the consequent stockpile and shortage quantities so as to minimize the total expenditure.
